dct_description_sm: This multi-year project aimed to perform a risk assessment and a vulnerability assessment of all Yukon Government-owned infrastructures. The objectives of the project were specifically: (1) to develop baseline knowledge on climatic conditions, permafrost, and infrastructure by collecting background information on parameters and by developing an inventory of infrastructure; (2) to conduct an Infrastructure Risk and Vulnerability Assessment; (3) to identify adaptation strategies that consider the changing climate and capacity of infrastructure; and (4) communicate information on permafrost and infrastructure between multi-disciplinary teams and other stakeholders.   In the project's first year, the focus was placed on the inventory of knowledge. In its second year, the project aimed: (1) to complete a Yukon Infrastructure Risk and Vulnerability Assessment to aid in adaptation measures relating to permafrost degradation and other climate change risks (i.e. sea level and temperature rises); (2) to evaluate the capacity of Government of Yukon owned/managed buildings in terms of current and projected future climate and permafrost conditions; and - (4) to provide recommendations for adaptation, as well as methods and standards for future infrastructure design and construction
